sub_scenario.family: review and decision quality under interruption density versus protected focused work
sub_scenario.one_line: supply allocation analyst: set an exception-only interruption rule

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the allocation sheet and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The carrier dashboard review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can answer a warehouse status call while updating a simple count.
Does live communication always reduce your accuracy?
No, not when the answer does not require balancing scarce stock.
Someone new shadowed me in the planning pod this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the shortage cycles into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
I did a standard pass over the carrier dashboard records this morning.
Any exceptions in there?
None worth a note.
I can make a quick route adjustment during a normal morning.
What kind of change is that?
One truck, one destination, and a clear spare capacity figure.
I archived last cycle's notes on the carrier dashboard and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
I confirmed next week's carrier dashboard slots with the team.
Any conflicts?
None that survived five minutes.
A vendor call about the allocation sheet ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the planning pod checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the shortage cycles.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the carrier dashboard records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
I closed a routine shortage cycles cycle without surprises.
Follow-up needed?
A note for the next cycle, nothing more.
I sketched next week's plan for the shortage cycles before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the allocation sheet updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I moved my reminders so the allocation sheet review lands before the weekly sync.
Small automation helps.
It adds up over a quarter.
I compared two options for the carrier dashboard tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the planning pod handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
What interruption rule should I set while allocating the remaining formula across clinics?

query: What interruption rule should I set while allocating the remaining formula across clinics?

ev_A.fact: During the pediatric formula shortage, I muted alerts for ninety minutes, reconciled clinic minimums against carrier limits, and assigned the remaining pallets without leaving any rural clinic below its floor.

ev_B.fact: In last spring's saline shortage, five pop-up messages arrived as I moved quantities between regions, so I followed the latest request rather than the minimum-coverage table and shorted one clinic.

E1.fact: I have asked dispatch to page me only for a vehicle breakdown or a safety hold while I am assigning constrained inventory.

E2.fact: Dispatch can route ordinary delivery questions to the dashboard and call me once after the allocation is locked.

relational_connector.relation: A protected reconciliation produced fair minimum coverage, while interruption-driven reallocations displaced a clinic below its agreed floor.

retrieval_cue.why_it_naturally_retrieves_R: A realistic work request forces a personalized decision without naming either episode or the relation between them.

relation_specificity.nearby_relation: The user can handle simple status calls and isolated route changes.
relation_specificity.why_it_does_not_license_C: Those tasks do not require preserving a multi-clinic scarcity calculation across competing requests.

coactivation_bridge: A shows the operating condition; B shows the demand or failure that makes it decisive. A protected reconciliation produced fair minimum coverage, while interruption-driven reallocations displaced a clinic below its agreed floor. E1 and E2 calibrate the practical recommendation without opening a second route to the conclusion.

latent_C.inference: Use a protected allocation interval with escalation only for transport or safety exceptions.

answer_contract.target_proposition: Use a protected allocation interval with escalation only for transport or safety exceptions.

decision_semantics.yes: The visible records support the target proposition.
decision_semantics.no: The visible records do not support the target proposition; this does not assert the opposite arrangement is good.
